text:
Jason Zucker's season started late and hasn't really started since. He had sports hernia surgery in the offseason, made his debut on Oct. 21, and has two goals and no assists in 14 games. This is the last year of his contract, coming off 24 goals and 45 points in 62 games for a Sabres team that finally broke its playoff drought, so the timing is cruel.

The ice time tells the story Buffalo fans are worried about. He is down almost four minutes a night over his last ten, with games of 7.7 and 9.7 minutes last week, and at five on five the Sabres get only about 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays.

Yet the process isn't all gone. His own expected goals per 60, 1.37, is right where it was last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 80th-percentile rate. Buffalo has scored 9.8 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. Our range still has him near 29 points if the minutes return.
